title: Physical Training Theory | TRX
subtitle: TRX, said to have originated with the Navy SEALs, stands for Total Resistance Exercise. It is, in fact, a suspension training system.
body:
## Introduction

TRX (the suspension training system), also called total resistance exercise, refers to a particular form of suspension training using equipment developed by former U.S. Navy SEAL Randy Hetrick. It uses bodyweight exercises to develop strength, balance, flexibility, and core stability simultaneously. It requires a TRX suspension trainer, a performance training tool that uses the exerciser’s own weight. TRX’s designers say it draws on research from military, professional sports, and academic institutions, as well as the TRX team’s experience “working with thousands of athletes, coaches, trainers, first responders, subject-matter experts, professors, and service members of every branch.”

## Advantages

TRX can be seen as a device that extends bodyweight training. Besides convenience, its characteristic advantage is creating an unstable movement environment, forcing the exerciser to recruit more muscle groups. This helps burn fat, train often-neglected stabilizing and smaller muscles, and improve the body’s ability to operate on unstable surfaces.

TRX’s greatest advantage is its compact portability and almost nonexistent requirements for a training space. You can complete a workout without leaving home, in a dorm room or hotel. All you need is a door to anchor it. (So if a city goes into lockdown, you can keep training at home: as long as life goes on, exercise goes on.)

Another advantage of TRX is that in the later stages of some exercises, the elasticity of the straps can assist in completing the proper movement, or help generate force when the lowest point of a movement is difficult.

## Origins

In the 1980s, a towel made of high-density fibers entered soldiers’ individual supply kits. Strong enough to support hundreds of pounds, it was often looped around a tank barrel so soldiers could grip both ends for pull-ups, or tied around an ammunition box to make a homemade kettlebell for curls and other movements.

After the turn of the century, the U.S. military developed a new suspension training system from this basis. A few straps could maintain training intensity in wartime while causing very few injuries, avoiding noncombat losses. Later, a U.S. **Navy SEAL** commander named Randy Hetrick redesigned the equipment and training plan after retirement, turning it into a civilian fitness program: the **TRX Suspension Training System**.

The five major physical qualities correspond to physiology and sports training theory; the kinetic chain corresponds to anatomy and sports biomechanics; functionality corresponds to physiology and biomechanics. The pyramid corresponds to all of them! Or rather, the pyramid is the intersection of these disciplines in physical training: it encompasses all the preceding theories and gives them deeper meaning.

## Principles

First, as a form of **unstable suspension training**, TRX places substantial demands on **core stability**. Whether you are doing planks, push-ups, or other common fitness movements, once transferred to TRX they train your core stabilizers through the straps, giving you strong waist and abdominal muscles. This is why many people find their abdomen and waist extremely sore the day after using TRX at the gym, even though they did not separately train their abs the previous day.

Second, TRX can be a training method for every part of the body. Chest, shoulders, back, arms, legs, or abs: the strength of every muscle can be fully trained.

Finally, TRX provides not only stability and strength training, but also **aerobic expenditure**, helping you burn fat.

## Carrying & Installation

Besides training the whole body, the TRX system’s greatest feature is being light and easy to carry. It fits entirely into a small drawstring bag, taking up little space or weight. Compared with heavy dumbbells, TRX is practically a magical tool for business travelers.

![TRX carrying bag](/img/Train-20200229-1.jpg "The TRX bag is about the size of an iPad box")

More importantly, TRX’s various anchor designs make it especially easy to suspend. You can train anywhere, and only a small area of movement space is needed.

![The complete TRX set](/img/Train-20200229-2.jpg "The complete TRX set")
